import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Read the data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a comprehensive dashboard with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Income Distribution by Education Level
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
education_order = ['PhD', 'Graduation', 'Master', '2n Cycle', 'Basic']
education_present = [e for e in education_order if e in df['Education'].unique()]
sns.boxplot(data=df, y='Education', x='Income', order=education_present, palette='Set2', ax=ax1)
ax1.set_title('Income Distribution by Education', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Income ($)', fontsize=9)
ax1.set_ylabel('Education', fontsize=9)

# 2. Spending by Category
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
spending_means = df[spending_cols].mean()
categories = ['Wines', 'Fruits', 'Meat', 'Fish', 'Sweets', 'Gold']
colors = plt.cm.Spectral(np.linspace(0, 1, len(categories)))
ax2.bar(categories, spending_means, color=colors, edgecolor='black', linewidth=1.5)
ax2.set_title('Average Spending by Product Category', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_ylabel('Average Amount Spent ($)', fontsize=9)
ax2.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax2.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 3. Purchase Channel Distribution
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
purchase_channels = {
    'Web': df['NumWebPurchases'].sum(),
    'Catalog': df['NumCatalogPurchases'].sum(),
    'Store': df['NumStorePurchases'].sum(),
    'Deals': df['NumDealsPurchases'].sum()
}
colors_pie = ['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4', '#45B7D1', '#FFA07A']
ax3.pie(purchase_channels.values(), labels=purchase_channels.keys(), autopct='%1.1f%%',
        colors=colors_pie, startangle=90)
ax3.set_title('Purchase Distribution by Channel', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')

# 4. Age Distribution
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
df['Age'] = 2024 - df['Year_Birth']
ax4.hist(df['Age'], bins=20, color='steelblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax4.set_title('Age Distribution of Customers', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Age', fontsize=9)
ax4.set_ylabel('Frequency', fontsize=9)
ax4.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 5. Income vs Total Spending
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
df['TotalSpending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)
scatter = ax5.scatter(df['Income'], df['TotalSpending'], c=df['Age'], 
                     cmap='viridis', alpha=0.6, edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax5.set_title('Income vs Total Spending', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Income ($)', fontsize=9)
ax5.set_ylabel('Total Spending ($)', fontsize=9)
cbar = plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax5)
cbar.set_label('Age', fontsize=8)
ax5.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 6. Campaign Acceptance Rate
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
campaigns = ['AcceptedCmp1', 'AcceptedCmp2', 'AcceptedCmp3', 'AcceptedCmp4', 'AcceptedCmp5', 'Response']
acceptance_rates = [df[camp].mean() * 100 for camp in campaigns]
campaign_labels = ['Cmp1', 'Cmp2', 'Cmp3', 'Cmp4', 'Cmp5', 'Response']
colors_bar = plt.cm.RdYlGn(np.linspace(0.3, 0.9, len(campaigns)))
ax6.barh(campaign_labels, acceptance_rates, color=colors_bar, edgecolor='black', linewidth=1.5)
ax6.set_title('Campaign Acceptance Rates', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_xlabel('Acceptance Rate (%)', fontsize=9)
ax6.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3)

# 7. Family Composition
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
ax7.bar(range(len(marital_counts)), marital_counts.values, 
        color='coral', edgecolor='black', linewidth=1.5)
ax7.set_xticks(range(len(marital_counts)))
ax7.set_xticklabels(marital_counts.index, rotation=45, ha='right')
ax7.set_title('Marital Status Distribution', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax7.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=9)
ax7.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 8. Recency Distribution
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
ax8.hist(df['Recency'], bins=20, color='mediumseagreen', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax8.set_title('Customer Recency (Days Since Last Purchase)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax8.set_xlabel('Recency (Days)', fontsize=9)
ax8.set_ylabel('Frequency', fontsize=9)
ax8.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 9. Correlation Heatmap (subset of key variables)
ax9 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
corr_vars = ['Income', 'TotalSpending', 'Recency', 'NumWebPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases']
corr_matrix = df[corr_vars].corr()
sns.heatmap(corr_matrix, annot=True, fmt='.2f', cmap='coolwarm', 
            center=0, square=True, ax=ax9, cbar_kws={'shrink': 0.8})
ax9.set_title('Key Variables Correlation', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax9.tick_params(axis='both', labelsize=8)

# Overall title
fig.suptitle('Customer Marketing Analytics Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
plt.close()
